summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is kept: neuropathy trials (pooled pain reduction 20.2% vs placebo in 31118753; very-low-certainty Cochrane evidence in diabetic neuropathy) and the MCI/early Alzheimer meta-analysis. The record claims Focus & Mental Clarity. The only source in cognitively healthy people (Cochrane 2017) found no usable evidence, the Cochrane dementia review found no objective cognitive benefit, and the one positive MCI/AD meta-analysis (2003) is abstract-only in a disease population. The neuropathy sources (one verified in full text, pain -20.2% vs placebo) are off-claim and partly intramuscular. No source meets the credit rule, so the record becomes reference-only, which removes ALCAR Evidence points from dependent products (about 40 per the closure plan).

identity.preparation: Acetyl-L-carnitine; intramuscular and oral phases differ and are not automatically equivalent.

population.description: Adults with painful peripheral neuropathy (diabetic, antiretroviral-toxic, chemotherapy-induced, carpal tunnel); 14 clinical trials reviewed; pooled pain analysis of 4 placebo-controlled RCTs in diabetic and antiretroviral neuropathy (Sima 2005 two cohorts, De Grandis 2002, Youle 2007).

study_contexts.study_design: PRISMA systematic review (to April 2018) of trials with >=10 neuropathy patients, AAN evidence classes, and random-effects meta-analysis of 4 placebo-controlled RCTs on 10-cm VAS pain.

outcomes.name: Pooled pain reduction versus placebo 20.2% of baseline VAS (95% CI 8.3-32.1%), P<0.0001, I2 62.8%; diabetic subgroup 24.6%.

limitations: Do not transfer intramuscular findings or uncontrolled regeneration measures into generic oral efficacy.
Cancer-treatment neuropathy prevention and possible harm must be evaluated separately; no broad neuroprotection approval.
Returned decision: Date-restricted hold. Publication-age-only exclusions were withdrawn and are not adopted.

The pooled pain contribution is four RCTs represented by three primary papers: Sima reports two trial cohorts. Wider uncontrolled and animal citations are not included as affirmative pooled trial dependencies.

Historical bibliography census (not independent scoring sources; actual included-publication membership is separately bound to the inspected source table): 15616239, 12455197, 17461852. Each intervention and comparison requires its own applicability assessment; citation in this bibliography grants no credit.

Included-study identifiers are now bound to this source's actual included-study rows/explicit inclusion references (Table1 author/year rows mapped to bibliography15,24–26,28–32,34–36,41; narrative negative chemotherapy-prevention studies37–39 included separately. Two Sima cohorts share one publication; no primary rat/mechanism papers borrowed. TableSheyu2016 corresponds to LiS/SheyuLi2016,232participants, as source26.), with live NIH title/content identity checks. They are publication pointers, not independent-cohort counts, per-primary-study scoring approvals, preparation equivalence or new efficacy evidence. Exact unindexed source citations remain retained; no missing PMID is invented.
No credit: painful neuropathy is not this record's Focus & Mental Clarity claim, two pooled trials used an intramuscular phase, and authors report Sigma-Tau/Alfasigma funding relationships.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: Trial-specific: Sima 500 or 1,000 mg three times daily for 1 year; De Grandis 1,000 mg/day IM for 10 days then 2,000 mg/day orally; Youle 500 mg IM twice daily for 14 days then 1,000 mg oral sachets twice daily for 42 days (Results; Table 1).
co_therapies: Background diabetes, HIV/antiretroviral or cancer treatment differs by trial.
dose.reported_regimen: Pooled RCT regimens 1,000-3,000 mg/day ALC, oral or intramuscular-then-oral, 2 weeks to 13 months (Table 1; Results).

normalization.basis: Preserve the specifically identified material or component quantity; no elemental/marker conversion or extrapolated daily dose.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC6498091): Methods, Table 1 (trial regimens), Results diabetic/HIV/chemotherapy sections, meta-analysis paragraph and Table 2, Discussion, competing interests.

clinical_review.notes: Directly addresses the record's Focus & Mental Clarity claim in cognitively healthy people and finds no usable evidence; supports no credit.

limitations: Cochrane 2017: only 2 RCTs in young healthy adults; no effect of L-carnitine on reaction time, vigilance, immediate memory or delayed recall after 3 days (about 200 participants); very low quality; authors could draw no conclusion. Abstract only; full text not retrieved.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

clinical_review.notes: Dementia treatment is not the record's focus claim, and the Cochrane review found no objective cognitive benefit; supports no credit.

limitations: Cochrane 2003: 11 double-blind RCTs, all Alzheimer's disease; Clinical Global Impression improved at 12 and 24 weeks (OR 2.33 and 3.91) but not at 52 weeks, and no benefit on cognition, dementia severity, function or CGI as a continuous measure. Abstract only.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

clinical_review.notes: Positive MCI/mild-AD meta-analysis, but abstract-only (route and included trials not verifiable), disease population rather than general focus, and contradicted on objective cognition by the later Cochrane review; no credit.

limitations: 2003 meta-analysis: double-blind placebo-controlled trials >=3 months in MCI and mild AD, 1.5-3.0 g/day; integrated effect size 0.201 (95% CI 0.107-0.295) and CGI-CH 0.32 (0.18-0.47). Full text not retrieved.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

clinical_review.notes: Diabetic neuropathy pain is off-claim and the Cochrane review rates it very low certainty; no credit.

limitations: Cochrane 2019: 4 studies, 907 participants; pain VAS MD -9.16 mm (-16.76 to -1.57) versus placebo, very low certainty; no difference at <=1500 mg/day; safety could not be judged. Abstract only.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

freshness_search.database: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities esearch, sort=pub_date, retmax=60; titles via esummary, abstracts via efetch)
freshness_search.query: (acetyl-L-carnitine[tiab] OR acetylcarnitine[tiab] OR "acetyl carnitine"[tiab] OR ALCAR[tiab]) AND (cognit* OR memory OR dementia OR Alzheimer* OR "mild cognitive impairment" OR attention OR fatigue OR depress*) AND (meta-analysis[pt] OR systematic review[pt] OR randomized controlled trial[pt]) AND 2015:2026[dp]
freshness_search.screening_rule: Kept syntheses and RCTs of ALCAR alone on cognition, attention or mental energy. Excluded L-carnitine (non-acetyl) exercise trials, multi-ingredient formulations, metabolomics and psychiatric-guideline overviews. Depression and hepatic-encephalopathy reviews were read as off-claim context.

read.title: Acetyl-L-carnitine Slows the Progression from Prefrailty to Frailty in Older Subjects: A Randomized Interventional Clinical Trial.
read.finding: 2022 RCT (the authors call it 'randomized, observational'), 92 pre-frail older adults, ALCAR 1.5 g twice daily for 3 months: MMSE and 6-min walk improved vs placebo. Single trial in a pre-frail elderly population.

read.title: Acetyl-L-Carnitine Supplementation and the Treatment of Depressive Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
read.finding: 2018 MA, 12 RCTs (791): depressive symptoms SMD -1.10 vs placebo (I2 86%). Depression is outside the record's claim.

read.title: Acetyl-L-carnitine for patients with hepatic encephalopathy.
read.finding: 2019 Cochrane review of ALCAR for hepatic encephalopathy (5 RCTs). A disease population outside the claim.

freshness_search.conclusion: confirms: no newer synthesis tests ALCAR for focus or cognition in cognitively healthy adults. The newer positive findings come from pre-frail elderly (one trial), depression or hepatic encephalopathy, all outside the Focus & Mental Clarity claim. No-credit stands.
